entities.summary: Count Johan Christopher Toll was a Swedish statesman and soldier who played a crucial role in the governance of Sweden during the late 18th century. He was born in 1737, in the province of Småland, Sweden, and died on May 21, 1817. Toll's career was marked by his involvement in the establishment of the Swedish Empire's borders and his contributions to the development of the Swedish military. He served as the Governor of the province of Östergötland from 1777 to 1785 and later as the Lieutenant Governor of the province of Jemtland from 1785 to 1795. Toll's significance lies in his role as a key figure in the governance of Sweden during a period of significant political and military change. He was a strong advocate for the establishment of a strong central government and played a key role in the development of the Swedish military. Toll's legacy can be seen in the modern-day Swedish government and military, which continue to draw on the principles and policies he helped to establish.
